az_barks_canyon_wall.blurb: Barks Canyon Wall is a multipitch cliff on the Peralta side of the Superstition Mountains, east of Phoenix. It is the range's go-to destination for longer routes, with 14 climbs that are almost all trad and mostly three or four pitches. Grades run from the mid 5.6 range up to 5.11, but the bulk sit between 5.8 and 5.10, so there is plenty for a confident moderate leader. The volcanic rock is decent by Superstition standards, though not flawless, and protection is placed rather than bolted. Expect a real walk in over a ridge, big desert scenery, and a quiet day compared with roadside crags.
az_barks_canyon_wall.parking_note: Leave the car at the Peralta Trailhead lot at the end of Peralta Road (FR 77). It is reached from Highway 60 by about seven miles of dirt road.

az_diamond_buttress.blurb: Diamond Buttress is a short cliff holding a small cluster of routes in Queen Creek Canyon, on the south side of the highway just east of The Pond. It has 14 climbs, mostly sport with a few trad lines, running from easy fifth class to 5.12. The middle of the range, 5.10 to 5.11, has the most routes, with a handful of easier ones to warm up on. Climbs are short and quick to lap, and the rock has a good reputation for quality lines. The walk in drops to a wash, crosses a slab and ends under a belay spot beside a tree, and traffic noise carries down.

az_westworld_dome.blurb: Westworld Dome is a big granite dome in the West Stronghold of Cochise Stronghold, in the Dragoon Mountains of southeast Arizona. It carries 14 routes, mostly multipitch trad with a couple of aid lines and one sport route. Difficulty clusters strongly at 5.10, with a few 5.9s and 5.11s and a single 5.13 above them. The face changes character as you move across it: low-angle slab in places, steeper and overhanging elsewhere, so sticky shoes help. It is a backcountry day with a long walk to the base and a rough road to the trailhead, so plan a full outing.

az_pasta_slab.blurb: Pasta Slab is a small granite crag on the south side of Little Granite Mountain, in the desert north of Scottsdale. Its 14 climbs are mostly traditional with two sport routes, and they are gentle: nearly everything is 5.8 or easier, including several that barely climb beyond scramble difficulty. That makes it a sensible spot for beginners learning to place gear, or for a short easy day on slab and crack lines. The rock is chunky granite. You reach it on foot from the Granite Mountain trailhead by following the loop trail around to the south end, then a cairned path to the main wall.

az_the_wing.blurb: The Wing is a west-facing granite wall in the Point of Rocks section of the Granite Dells, near Prescott. It holds 14 routes, almost all trad with one sport line, and they are long and sustained rather than short. Grades start at 5.7 and mostly fall between 5.10 and 5.12, so it suits experienced leaders. Moderate lines follow cracks that take good gear, while the harder ones tend to smear up shallow grooves. Getting to the base can involve fourth-class scrambling in the canyon bottom for some routes, and a long rope and a double rack are worth bringing.
